overall: The AG found the Milford School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by not approving its January 15, 2019 minutes in a timely manner; claims about posting, location, and summary were rejected or not reached.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to create and approve minutes of its January 15, 2019 meeting in a timely manner.
Complainant argued the January 15 minutes were late because they were not posted to the school website while later minutes were.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law only requires that minutes be created, reviewed, and approved in a timely manner; it does not require that meeting minutes be posted to a website.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 15 minutes did not identify the location of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes remain in draft form and have not yet been approved. Because the minutes may still be amended, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law for insufficiency of meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 15 minutes lacked an adequate summary of the discussion held at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes may still be amended, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law for insufficiency of meeting minutes.

remedy: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Review and approve the minutes of the January 15 meeting within 30 days of receipt of the letter and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
